title: observability: propagate request-id & trace across API surface, add structured logs and per-endpoint metric tags (OpenAI compat)
author: Maya Patel
description: Motivation: Customers and platform teams have requested consistent observability across our API surface (hosted, dedicated, and private). This change ensures a single request identifier is propagated end-to-end, W3C trace context is forwarded and correlated, logs are emitted in structured JSON with enrichment, and per-endpoint metric tags are added for more granular cost/latency breakdowns. This also brings the OpenAI compatibility layer up-to-date so third-party SDKs that rely on request_id/traceparent behaviors work with Redwood. Summary of changes: - Accept and honor external request id headers (X-Redwood-Request-Id, X-Request-Id, request_id) and prefer incoming id when present; generate a v4 UUID when absent. - Propagate W3C trace context (traceparent / tracestate) through gateway -> router -> serving runtime; attach trace_id to spans and logs. - Emit structured JSON logs from API gateway, router, and handler layers. Logs include: timestamp, level, service, env, request_id, trace_id, route, model, client_id (when available), user_agent, and request_latency_ms. - Streaming: add a 'meta' control event as the first SSE/chunked response that includes request_id and traceparent so consumers can correlate streaming responses. Ensure request_id is attached to each chunk's metadata payload. - Function/tool calling & structured output: when tools/functions are invoked during generation, produced logs and metrics include the originating request_id/trace_id and the tool name. - Per-endpoint metric tags: metrics emitted to StatsD/Prometheus have tags: route, api_compat (openai/redwood), model, and deployment_mode (hosted/dedicated/private). - OpenAI compatibility: the compatibility shim normalizes request_id and traceparent headers, mirrors required response headers where appropriate, and documents the differences in behavior. Checklist: - [x] Header parsing and normalization in API gateway - [x] W3C trace context propagation through router and runtime proxies - [x] Structured logger added (JSON) with minimal allocation overhead - [x] Streaming meta event implemented and tested - [x] Metric tagging for routes + tests - [x] Tests: unit + integration + streaming e2e - [x] Docs: developer notes and openai-compat migration notes Rollout plan: feature gated by runtime flag 'observability.request_propagation_v1'. Canary rollout to 5% of traffic for 48h with increased sampling of traces; monitor latency and error budgets in Redwood Console. If any regression in streaming latencies >5th percentile, automatic rollback. Compatibility notes: - For existing customers using our OpenAI compatibility layer, we now echo X-Redwood-Request-Id in responses when provided by client. This is additive and non-breaking. - Tooling that depends on older non-W3C trace headers should be updated to use traceparent. Testing: - Added unit tests for header normalization, trace propagation, structured log fields. - Integration tests between gateway and runtime that assert trace id continuity. - Streaming e2e test asserts first meta event and presence of request_id on subsequent chunks. CI: all checks passed (build, unit, integration, streaming e2e, linters).

review_comments: Lena Torres: Nice end-to-end story. Please add a note about potential increased cardinality in metrics and add a sampling strategy for low-cardinality aggregates.
Maya Patel (author): Addressed — added per-model sampling and default cardinality caps in metrics_sink (see commit e3f1b57).
Arjun Mehta: The structured logger looks good, but watch allocations on hot paths. Can we reuse buffers from a pool?
Maya Patel: Yes — jsonlogger uses a sync.Pool and preallocated buffer per goroutine; added benchmark numbers in comment and test.
Samir Kaur: Streaming meta event is great. How will SDKs surface this?
Maya Patel: SDKs will expose a 'meta' event from the stream parser; compatibility shim documents mapping. Added an example in docs.
Lena Torres: Approved after the metrics cardinality change and added tests.
notes_on_perf: Benchmarks show <2% median latency increase on gateway for header parsing and structured logging when enabled; 95th percentile unchanged. Streaming tail latency unchanged in canary. Metrics overhead limited by sampling settings.
release_notes: Added end-to-end request_id propagation and W3C trace context forwarding; structured JSON logs with enriched fields; per-endpoint metric tags; streaming meta event with request/trace IDs; OpenAI-compat shim updated to normalize tracing headers.
